title: Camera
blurb: Camera not found, black picture, blocked by privacy settings.

remedies.title: Camera doesn't work or shows black
remedies.why: The privacy shutter or camera key is off, privacy settings block apps, another app holds the camera, or the driver failed.

steps.text: Look for a sliding cover over the camera, or a camera key (often F8/F10) on the keyboard.
Allow camera access, and for desktop apps too.
Allow the app in Privacy & Security › Camera, then quit and reopen it.
Close every app that might use the camera (Teams, Zoom, browsers), then open the Camera app to test.
Close every app that might use the camera, then test in Photo Booth or FaceTime.
Check Device Manager › Cameras: if it shows a warning, right-click › Uninstall device, then restart.
For an external webcam, try another USB port without a hub.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT if the camera is missing from Device Manager or System Information (hardware fault or blocked by policy).

remedies.title: App uses the wrong camera
remedies.why: Apps pick the first camera they find: a laptop's built-in one, a virtual camera, or an iPhone (Continuity Camera).

steps.text: Choose the camera in the app's own settings (Teams: Device settings; Zoom: Video).
Turn off Continuity Camera on the iPhone (Settings › General › AirPlay & Continuity) if it keeps taking over.
Disable a camera you never use in Device Manager › Cameras.

remedies.title: Camera picture is blurry, dark or grainy
remedies.why: A smudged lens, light behind you, or low internet bandwidth (the app lowers quality).

steps.text: Wipe the lens with a soft cloth.
Face a window or lamp; avoid bright light behind you.
Turn on background blur sparingly; it can lower quality on slower computers.
Check the quality in the Camera app: if it's good there, the meeting app is lowering it for the connection.

remedies.title: Camera light turns on by itself
remedies.why: An app (often a meeting app or browser tab in the background) is using the camera. Rarely, unwanted software.

steps.text: See which app uses it: Settings › Privacy & security › Camera shows apps that used the camera recently.
The green dot in the menu bar (and Control Center) names the app using the camera.
Turn off camera access for apps that don't need it.
If an app you don't know is using it, run a full virus scan and tell IT.
